THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
 1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 23.11.2018  PASSED IN MVC NO.50/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDITIONAL  DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT  CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BELAGAVI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF  COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
Master Preetam @ Preeyatam Basavaraj vs The Chairman Shri. Basaveshwar Multi on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82902849/
1  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11477  MFA No. 103488 of 2019  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the injured claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 23.11.2018, passed in MVC No.50/2017 on the file of the I-Addl.
District and Sessions Judge & Addl. MACT, Belagavi.

entities.text:
I-Addl.
District and Sessions Judge & Addl. MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri. D.T. Hebbar, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation of Rs.2,07,595/-, which is contrary to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another1.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks to re- assess the same by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Shri S.S. Koliwad for respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal taking note of aforesaid judgment in Master Mallikarjun referred to supra, has awarded just and proper compensation,
which does not call for any enhancement.
Thus, seeks dismissal of appeal.
I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the material available on record.

5. The pleadings and evidence on record indicate that Master Preetam @ Preeyatam Basavaraj Balagappanavar met with a road traffic accident on 20.09.2016 and sustained fractures indicated in the Wound Certificate at Ex.P10, which is not disputed by the parties to the proceedings.
In support of the claim, two witnesses were examined namely, father of minor claimant as PW1 and the Doctor namely Dr. B.F. Patil, Ortho, as PW2.
The medical evidence on record indicates that the appellant has sustained disability to the whole body and taking note of the same this Court assess the disability at 11%.

Applying the principles laid down in Master Mallikarjun's case referred to supra,
this Court re-assesses the compensation as under:
1. Pain and suffering and loss of Rs.3,00,000/-
 amenities Discomfort,
 inconvenience & loss of earnings  2. To the parents during Rs.25,000/-
 hospitalization  3.

Medical and incidental expenses Rs.57,595/-
 TOTAL Rs.3,82,595/-

sentences.text:
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal stands partly allowed.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,82,595/-
as against Rs.2,07,595/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

(iv) The respondent/Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(v) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
(vi) Draw modified award accordingly.
(vii) No order as to costs.

Sd/-
(VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) JUDGE VNP, CT:VP Master Preetam @ Preeyatam Basavaraj vs The Chairman Shri. Basaveshwar Multi on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82902849/
